evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: Arden: 'Upon checking we still have availability for Wednesday the thirtieth, so in order for me to build an estimated quote for you I need to ask a few questions that might take around ten to fifteen minutes. Would that be fine?' [promised time-box and quote, but no wait for explicit yes — customer says 'Yes' but only after clarifying whose move it is, and Arden immediately pivots into clarification questions instead of a clean acknowledge-and-proceed]
evidence_quotes.their_agenda: Never asked. Arden jumps directly into logistics probing (clarifying packing vs. loading, confirming details from online form) without ever asking 'Other than price, what are your biggest concerns about this move?'
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: N/A — no concerns were raised by the customer in a section meant for them to set their own agenda. The crisis (foreclosure, deadline) emerged naturally during logistics conversation, not in response to an 'agenda' question.
evidence_quotes.active_listening_reflection: N/A — no summary reflection offered. Arden acknowledged the foreclosure/deadline situation with empathetic murmurs ('I'm sorry to hear') but never reflected back 'So what I'm hearing is ________, ________ and ________. Did I get all of it?'
evidence_quotes.logistics_details_gathered: Full — property type (house, 1-story), floor/stories (one story), number of rooms (3 bedrooms), walking distance (storage unit is nearby, driveway accessible), additional rooms (garage with tools/woodworking, no separate balcony/storage mentioned beyond garage), special considerations (piano, antiques, appliances, foreclosure deadline), additional stops (garage, storage unit on second floor with elevator). All seven items covered.
evidence_quotes.packing_services_offered: True — offered multiple times: 'Do you want help packing?' and confirmed 'full packing' of entire home.
evidence_quotes.box_count_asked: True — 'Typically ma'am for a house this size box count is within 45 to 55... do you think we're gonna be exceeding 55?' Customer said 'more than fifty boxes,' Arden estimated 80.
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor: Full — Arden gave a typical range (6–8 hours for a house this size for two movers), then personalized it: 'However miss robin in your case... since you also requested for full packing of the entire home into a second floor storage unit... I'm estimating the move to take around eight and a half to nine and a half hours for four movers in two truck and it's good to budget an overall of $3,948.' Also offered 6-mover comparison ($4,044 for 6.5 hrs).
evidence_quotes.pricing_framing: Full — Trip fee/overnight fee transparency: not explicitly stated. However, Arden did frame: (1) hourly rate ($96/person, $384 for 4 movers), (2) 'no hidden fee, no credit card fee, no transportation fee, no terrible fees, no disassemble or reassembly fees,' (3) '2.5 hour minimum,' (4) 'once we go over the minimum the time will be paraded in fifteen minutes increment,' (5) no deposit required. All key framing present; trip/overnight fees not explicitly disclosed but structure is transparent.
evidence_quotes.feels_fair_then_silence: Not asked — Arden never asked 'Does that feel fair?' or equivalent, and never held a genuine pause for customer processing. Instead, Arden immediately pivoted to next steps and comparisons: 'However, miss Becky that is just an estimate... if it's gonna be for six movers... it's almost just the same amount...'. No silence held.
evidence_quotes.on_time_guarantee_delivered: Full — 'We also have an on time guarantee. So, if the movers arrive late, you start to get discount on your final bill ma'am.'
evidence_quotes.damage_coverage_delivered: Full — 'once you book it is a free evaluation coverage that gives you up to $2,000 for this move. If anything gets damaged, gets broken you can just give us a call to file a claim zero deductible... gonna repair, replace or reimburse that within three to five business days.' The $2,000 coverage, no deductible, and no fine-print framing were all delivered clearly.
evidence_quotes.closes_the_loop: False — Arden never asked 'Does that put those to rest?' or equivalent after delivering the Two Promises. Instead, moved directly into 'We do not require any deposit. So once you book a, once you book it with us, movers will just come and you only pay after the actual move is done.'
evidence_quotes.final_concerns_check: Throwaway — Arden asked 'Before we get into that, do you have any question? Any clarification regarding the moving process in general?' and 'Now if that's the case then ma'am, I think I'm all good with my estimate. So, I'm going to be sending four movers and two trucks tomorrow... do you have a questions clarification so I can explain the pricing?' These are empty 'any questions?' statements, not genuine concern-reopening like 'What's still concerning you about this move?'
evidence_quotes.catch_all_asked: False — Arden never asked 'Anything coming with you we haven't talked about?' or equivalent.
evidence_quotes.explicit_ask: Never — Arden never asked 'Would you like our help with your move?' or a direct booking request. Instead, the call ended with Arden saying 'Of course, ma'am, I'll send you an email ma'am' and offering to send quotes via email. The customer said she'd call her brother and get back. No explicit 'Would you like to book?' was asked.
evidence_quotes.rate_lock_mentioned: False — No mention of rate lock or guarantee that the quote holds.
evidence_quotes.booking_confirmed: None — No booking occurred. Customer left to consult her brother. No date, phone, arrival window, crew size, or addresses confirmed for an actual booking.

top_strength: Arden gathered comprehensive logistics details, handled a deeply emotional and urgent situation (foreclosure, 24-hour deadline) with genuine empathy and reassurance, and delivered both of the Two Promises (On-Time Guarantee and No Worries Damage Coverage) fully and clearly.
coaching_note: Never asked the customer's own agenda for concerns ('Other than price, what are your biggest concerns about this move?'), skipped the critical 'Does that feel fair?' pause after the estimate, and most critically — never asked for the business ('Would you like our help with your move?'), ending instead with 'I'll send you an email' and no booking confirmation at all.
